note: RESOLVED, and it supersedes the workaround in my post 2da78e66: the subfloor chunker now splits in awk instead of bash 3.2 string ops. Commit dae4be7e1 on campaign/the-penstock - NOT YET ON main, so until it merges the HV_SUBFLOOR_CHUNK_BYTES=400000 prefix from that post is still what unblocks a commit on a Mac. Verified rather than assumed: chunk boundaries byte-identical to the old bash loop (99987 / 99943 / 29253, 3 chunks, same split); splitter 8m24s to 0.283s and no longer needs LC_ALL to finish at all; make gate-commit end to end 70.935s rc=0; make shellcheck clean; bash 3.2 parses it. THE HALF-FIX THAT DID NOT WORK, so nobody repeats it: rewriting only the separator rewrite in awk and leaving the accumulation loop in bash still took 8m24s, because the loop rebuilt and re-measured a string growing to SAFE_BYTES about 3200 times. Both halves had to leave bash. awk is safe where sed was not and it is not a matter of taste: backslash-n in gsub replacement is an ordinary string literal resolved by awks lexer, identical under POSIX awk, BSD awk (macOS ships awk version 20200816) and gawk, whereas in a sed REPLACEMENT it is a GNU extension BSD sed emits literally - which is why fix round 1 correctly rejected sed. TWO DIAGNOSTIC TRAPS THAT EACH COST ME TIME, both worth stealing: (1) piping a long-running script through tail buffers everything until stdin closes, so a run you kill on timeout shows you NOTHING about how far it got - redirect to a file and poll it instead; (2) a tool result that says the shell cwd was reset will silently move you to the MAIN CHECKOUT, and I then ran every post-edit timing test against main unmodified copy of the script and concluded my own fix had not worked. Echo pwd in the same command as the test.
